raw_response:
Let me think through this as the farmer would, in her own voice.

---

*Thinking as the farmer:*

Three mu. That's what we have. My husband goes to town for work some weeks, and my oldest boy helps when he's not at his factory job. Seven mouths at home — my mother-in-law, the little ones, all of us. The wheat and the maize, that's what feeds us. The maize we sell a little, the wheat mostly we keep and grind.

I've been doing this the same way for many years. My mother did it like this, my neighbors do it like this. No point changing when it works.

**The wheat** — I plant after Cold Dew, when the weather turns. In October. I use seed from last year's harvest if it looked good; if not, I go to the shop in town. Before I plant, I put down compound fertilizer — one bag per mu, that's 50 jin. The man with the tractor comes and plows it in. Cost me about 60 yuan per mu for the plowing, but I can't do it by hand in time.

After winter, when the wheat is waking up, I walk the field and spread urea — about half a bag per mu, maybe a bit more if the wheat looks pale. Water three times: once before the ground freezes, once when the stalks start rising, and once when the grain is filling. The well water costs money, I don't water more than I need. If the sky gives rain, I skip.

Weeds I spray once in spring — a small bottle from the shop, cheap. Bugs I mostly don't bother unless I see a lot.

I hope for 700 jin per mu. Sometimes I get more, sometimes less. Last year was alright.

**The maize** — This is the hard part. When the wheat comes off in June, we have maybe five days. No time to plow. I borrow my cousin's hand planter and we push it down the rows, right into the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed from the shop — everyone uses hybrid now, I wouldn't save maize seed, it doesn't work right the next year. One bag of seed for the three mu, about 70 or 80 yuan.

I put a small handful of fertilizer in each hole when we plant, then when the maize is up to my knee I spread urea between the rows. Summer has rain usually, so maybe I water once, maybe twice if July is dry. If I see armyworm I'll spray, but last few years not much trouble.

Maize does better than wheat here if the summer is normal — 800 jin, 900 jin per mu sometimes. My daughter-in-law and I pick it by hand in September.

I don't spend money I don't have. If there's a good year, we save a little. If it's bad, we tighten. That's how it goes.
